deep.reconstruction:
This page proves a standard lemma from the theory of entire functions. It supports the previous page, which defines the 'order' of a sequence of complex numbers (the convergence exponent inf{s>0 : Σ|z_i|^s<∞}), compares the order of a genus-type product f(z)=∏(1+α_i z) with that of F built from |α_i|, and sketches extensions to sequences in Banach/Fréchet spaces and to bounded sets.

Setting: (r_ν) is an increasing sequence of positive reals tending to ∞. The counting function is n(r)=#{ν : r_ν ≤ r}, and α>0.

Formula (1), for 0≤a<b<∞: Σ_{a<r_ν<b} r_ν^{-α} = n(b−0)/b^α − n(a+0)/a^α + α∫_a^b n(r) r^{-α-1} dr. This is Abel summation written as a Stieltjes integration by parts: the left side is ∫_{(a,b)} r^{-α} dn(r).

Proposition: Σ r_ν^{-α}<∞ ⇔ ∫_0^∞ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr<∞. In that case n(r)/r^α→0 and the tail formula (1') holds: Σ_{r_ν>a} r_ν^{-α} = −n(a+0)/a^α + α∫_a^∞ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr.

Proof of ⇒: take a=0 to get (1 bis). Since n vanishes near 0, the boundary term at 0 disappears. The integral is then bounded by the partial sums.

Proof of ⇐: if the integral converges, n(r)/r^α cannot stay ≥ M for all large r, since otherwise the integral would dominate M∫dr/r. So there are b_i→∞ with n(b_i)/b_i^α ≤ M. The partial sums up to b_i are then bounded by M + α∫_0^∞ n/r^{α+1}.

The next page proves n(r)/r^α→0 by a block argument and generalizes to Σλ(r_ν) for decreasing C^1 λ. This is the classical fact that the convergence exponent of the zeros can be read off from n(r) (the Borel/Hadamard/Lindelöf setting). Its purpose is the larger programme on these pages: attaching an 'order' to sequences, operators and bounded sets in locally convex spaces. That programme resurfaces in Grothendieck's published work on nuclear operators of order p and on Fredholm determinants as entire functions of finite order.
errors: In (1') the summand is written 1/r_ν instead of 1/r_ν^α, a slip of the pen.
Formula (1) at a=0 contains the undefined term n(0+0)/0^α. It is harmless only because r_ν>0 forces n≡0 near 0; the author silently handles this in (1 bis).
In the ⇐ direction the existence of b_i with n(b_i)/b_i^α ≤ M is asserted without justification. The justification is easy: otherwise ∫ n r^{-α-1} ≥ M∫dr/r = ∞.
Minor: the crossed-out first attempt at ⇐ was abandoned. The final argument is correct.

ideas.what: Abel/Stieltjes summation linking Σ r_ν^{-α} with ∫ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr via the counting function
ideas.modern_name: Abel summation; convergence exponent of a sequence expressed through its counting function
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Abel; Borel, Hadamard, Lindelöf in entire function theory, ca. 1890–1905)
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material (e.g. Titchmarsh, Boas, Levin); Grothendieck only uses it implicitly

ideas.what: Order of a sequence/operator, used to control the order of an associated entire function (context from previous page)
ideas.modern_name: p-nuclear / Schatten-type order of operators; order of the Fredholm determinant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Produits tensoriels topologiques 1955; La théorie de Fredholm 1956)
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Mem. AMS 16, 1955), ch. II; 'La théorie de Fredholm', Bull. SMF 84 (1956)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but entirely classical Abel-summation lemma on counting functions and convergence exponents. It serves the 'order of a sequence/operator' programme, which Grothendieck did publish in his work on nuclear operators and Fredholm theory. Nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: In (1') the image indeed shows 1/r_ν without the exponent α; this is the author's slip, not a transcription error, but the intended exponent is α.
Line 1: the crossed-out word before '>0' is illegible; 'nombres réels' is plausible.
The lower limit in '∫_{r_0}^{b} r^{-α} dn(r)' is uncertain in the image; it may be 'a' (more consistent with formula (1)).
